summary: Independent review of candidate e7dff9af317bbfd5701e4c43f3b0b94f40c63a8b found the complete default-off NO_TOKEN lookahead design, including head-prefix lock reconciliation, bounded aging, post-pin chunk capacity reserve, priority-scheduling disable, and unchanged ordinary PrefillAdder gates. No functional counterexample was found in the available contract-test environment.

tests.what_was_measured: Reproduced that the waiting-queue admission loop unconditionally breaks after the queue head returns NO_TOKEN and that no lookahead module exists on the recorded base.
40 candidate regression and existing admission tests passed, covering the real simulated RadixCache contract and ordinary prefill gates.
Independent lock balance across rematch/head change/admission, bounded aging, exact post-pin reserve acceptance, and insufficient-reserve unwind.
sglang and prefill_lookahead imported from /job/repo/python/sglang at exact candidate commit, not from a stale wheel.
Available architecture was a single AMD Instinct MI350X gfx950 with ROCm 7.2; inventory only, not candidate GPU execution.

remaining_limitations: The reported prefill-only H100 TP=8 hierarchical-cache deployment was unavailable; its throughput, TTFT, idle-round, cache-hit, and production lock-balance percentages remain unverified.
Single-node CPU contract tests do not qualify distributed TP=8 timing or race behavior.
The candidate changes no native source, so no native rebuild was applicable; the prepared environment declares native=null and wheel=null.
The available GPU was AMD MI350X gfx950 rather than NVIDIA H100, and no model-weight serving workload was needed or run.
